pamphlet_excerpts: Need for Bird Study: Birds lend life, color, and music to the outdoors, and they are an important part of the ecosystems that keep thisplanet healthy (p. 10).
Need for Bird Study Principle 2: Because they are sensitive to changes in theenvironment, birds are valuable indicators of trouble, includingpollution and habitat loss (p. 10).
Need for Bird Study Principle 3: It was the near-disappearance of baldeagles, peregrine falcons, and brown pelicans decades ago thatalerted people to the dangers of many (p. 10).
Need for Bird Study Principle 4: Major, rapiddeclines in the number of songbirds have shown that we mustpreserve large areas for wildlife habitat (p. 10).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Need for Bird Study): Each species is lumped with its closest relatives to form a genus, usually on the basis of physical characteristicslike the shapes of certain bones (p. 10).
Step 2 (Need for Bird Study): Closely related genera (theplural of "genus") are grouped together to form a family (p. 10).
Step 3 (Need for Bird Study): Most field guides are arranged in this taxonomic order (p. 10).
Step 4 (Need for Bird Study): Because related birds often act and look somewhat the same, knowing these relationships can help you identify a new, puzzling species (p. 10).

Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: Famous scientists such as David Sibley are well known for their work in the field of ornithology (p. 52).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: Veterinarians and veterinarytechnicians can serve in the specializedfield of avian medicine and surgery (p. 52).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Volunteer activities may include bird census counting, monitoring the nesting sites of endangered species, andreporting hatchling survival (p. 52).
Step 2 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Many of these activities aremanaged by governmental agencies such as state and federalwildlife departments (p. 52).
Step 3 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Use a field notebook small enough to fit easily in a shirtpocket or outside compartment of a pack (p. 52).
Step 4 (Careers & Professional Pathways): You mightdecide to devote an entire page to one species of bird, noting itscolor, pattern, song, or behavior (p. 52).
